records.supported_name_scope: The complete generalized polygon has strong geographic correspondence with the western blue-water basin. Lake Ohrid is a low-confidence naming candidate from wording inside a partial conservation overlay, qualified by re-designate. The name coverage and authority for the complete water polygon remain unverified; no supported whole-water identity is assigned.
correspondence_observations: The complete 38-position north-south ring was considered, including the broad northern cap, northeast shoulder, long eastern shore, rounded southern end and west-side indentation.

The complete elongated western blue-water basin on the PONT map has the same broad configuration and regional placement, west of the Galicica mountain/park area and northwest of the two eastern lakes. The northern cap, eastern shoulder, southern end and western indentation were compared as a complete footprint.

The map prints Lake Ohrid with the parenthetical re-designate inside a conservation overlay covering the northern-country portion of this basin. This wording motivates the Lake Ohrid geographic candidate but does not directly label the entire water polygon. The separate Ohrid city symbol and city label on the northeastern shore are not used to establish the lake name.

Horizontal green hatching and diagonal conservation hatching cross the lake. Strong geographic correspondence uses the blue-water outer margin and regional arrangement, not the proposed-park, protected-landscape or international-border limits. Those observations do not resolve whole-waterbody name coverage or naming authority.
name_scope_limits: PONT is the Prespa Ohrid Nature Trust, a conservation trust/fund. Its own thematic map is useful cartographic evidence, but it is not a governmental naming authority, formal gazetteer or legal naming instrument.

One map provides the evidence. Its printed scale is 1:340,000. No reliable printed publication date was found; the 2021/11 URL directory is not treated as proof of a publication date. Current shoreline conditions and authoritative name variants were not established.

The source polygons are Natural Earth 1:10 million generalizations. All complete selected outlines were compared, but detailed bays, islands, marsh edges and fine shoreline offsets are outside the result.
Conservation-designation labels and boundaries have a different scope from lake names and water margins. Country borders across water do not partition the lake identity.

confidence.basis: Complete-outline visual comparison establishes geographic correspondence to the mapped basin. Geometric confidence must not be read as naming confidence.

correspondence_observations: The complete 58-position ring was considered, including the broad northwest head, irregular western embayments and projections, long eastern side, southeastern lobe and southwest-reaching arm.

The larger eastern blue-water basin on the PONT map has corresponding broad northern water, indented western shore, long eastern side and southwestern arm. It is east of the western lake and immediately northwest of the smaller southeastern lake. The complete blue-water footprint, including the long southwestern portion, was inspected.

The words Prespa Lake appear as part of the Prespa Lake Monument of Nature designation in the northern-country portion of the corresponding basin. The literal wording motivates a geographic candidate, but a conservation-area label does not directly name the entire water polygon or extend the designation across the international borders. Great Prespa is not separately printed as a waterbody name.

Complete-outline correspondence supports the geographic association with this larger eastern basin. The conservation-overlay label supplies a low-confidence Prespa Lake naming candidate only. Neither whole-waterbody name coverage, naming authority, exact named-lake extent nor a Great Prespa name form is established.

The smaller southeastern blue-water basin on the PONT map has the same broad head-and-southwestern-tail arrangement and lies southeast of the larger eastern lake. Both the head and the entire tapered southwestern reach were considered.

The nearby Prespa National Park (GR) label names a protected area. No distinct Small Prespa waterbody label was found over the complete smaller lake in this map. The map title and neighbouring park labels are not promoted to a lake name.

The source geometry and mapped water differ in fine shoreline shape and treatment of the southwestern reach. This is sufficient for a bounded generalized geographic comparison, but not a surveyed whole-lake shoreline or independently established Small Prespa name.
